text: Barriers to longitudinal connectivity (number of weirs/dams)
source: OAH Field Sampling Protocols (Zenodo 20344421), Annex I field form, section 3 hydromorphological characterization, p.13. The answer options are Firstline's.

text: Presence of other artificial structures occupying the stream banks, or margins
source: OAH Field Sampling Protocols (Zenodo 20344421), Annex I field form, section 3 hydromorphological characterization, p.13. The form continues 'up to 10m after the stream bank (specify, e.g. banks, street lights, sidewalks, bike paths, roads, houses, industrial facilities)'. The answer options are Firstline's.

text: Outflows (number of pipes or similar discharging pluvial waters to the stream)
source: OAH Field Sampling Protocols (Zenodo 20344421), Annex I field form, section 3 hydromorphological characterization, p.13. Mapping pipes to altered runoff (S03) is Firstline's reading, logged in DECISIONS.md. The answer options are Firstline's.

text: CC: concrete or similar artificial impervious materials
source: OAH Field Sampling Protocols (Zenodo 20344421), Annex I field form, section 3 'Substrate in the banks' (code CC), p.13. The form's own scale is A absent, P present, E extensive (more than 33% of the banks).

OAH Field Sampling Protocols (Zenodo 20344421), Annex I field form, section 3 'Substrate types present in the channel' (code AR), p.13. The form's own scale is A absent, P present, E extensive (more than 33% of the channel).
OAH Field Sampling Protocols (Zenodo 20344421), Annex I field form, section 3 'Flow types' (code D), p.13. The form's own scale is A absent, P present, E extensive (more than 33% of the channel).

OAH Field Sampling Protocols (Zenodo 20344421), Annex I field form, section 4a channel vegetation types, p.14 (abundance A/P/E; extensive is more than 33% of the channel). Algae as a sign of nutrient enrichment (S01) is Firstline's reading, informed by D2.4 p.42 ('excessive algal growth ... if nutrient inputs remain high'), logged in DECISIONS.md.

text: Is there litter or floating rubbish in or beside the stream?
source: Firstline-authored prompt; NOT in the OAH field form or the Key Indicators factsheets. Grounded in D2.4 p.30 (plastics under water pollution) and D2.4 p.127 (children learn to recognise litter as a key stressor).

text: Are the banks visibly eroded, slumping or undercut?
source: Firstline-authored prompt; NOT in the OAH field form or the Key Indicators factsheets. Grounded in D2.4 p.30 ('bank erosion and instability' under geomorphological changes).

text: Does the water smell of sewage, chemicals or oil?
source: Firstline-authored prompt; NOT in D2.4, the OAH field form or the Key Indicators factsheets. The least-grounded item: a lay proxy for D2.4 p.30 water pollution (organic matter, hydrocarbons).

text: Is the water cloudy, discoloured or foamy?
source: Firstline-authored prompt; NOT in the OAH field form or the Key Indicators factsheets. A lay proxy for D2.4 p.30 water pollution (suspended solids).
